# PIPE CLAMP WITH A SPRING-OPENED HINGED CAP

## BACKGROUND

<!-- src: disclosure:§1, item:O1 -->
The present disclosure relates to pipe clamps that hold a pipe, for example on a wall bracket.

<!-- src: disclosure:§1, disclosure:§8, item:O1 -->
A known pipe clamp on a wall bracket holds a pipe with two bolts, as in standard two-bolt pipe clamps according to DIN 3015. To add or remove a pipe, a fitter removes both bolts, holds the pipe with one hand and refits both bolts. On a ladder this takes two hands and often ends with a dropped bolt. Hinged hose clamps with a screw latch are also known.

## SUMMARY

<!-- src: feature:F1, item:O2 -->
In one aspect, a pipe clamp comprises a base having a saddle groove configured to receive a pipe, and a cap having a cap groove facing the saddle groove. A first side of the cap is pivotally connected to a first side of the base. A spring arranged between the base and the cap biases the cap away from the base toward an open position. A latch at a second side of the base is releasable and holds the cap in a closed position against the spring.

<!-- src: feature:F19, item:O2 -->
In another aspect, a method of securing a pipe in a clamp is provided. The clamp comprises a base having a saddle groove, a cap pivotally connected to the base by a hinge pin, and a spring biasing the cap away from the base. In the following order, the pipe is placed in the saddle groove, the cap is pivoted about the hinge pin onto the pipe, the spring is compressed with the cap, a locking pin is pushed through a latch lug of the base and a cap latch lug of the cap, and the cap is released, the locking pin then holding the cap closed against the spring.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

<!-- src: template, item:O4 -->
The following description refers to the drawings, in which the same reference numerals designate the same parts. The embodiments described are examples of the subject matter defined by the claims.

<!-- src: feature:F1, feature:F9, feature:F10, disclosure:§2, figure:FIG. 1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O5 -->
FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 show a pipe clamp 10 that holds a pipe 42. The pipe clamp 10 has a base and a cap 24. The base has a saddle groove 18 configured to receive the pipe 42. The cap 24 forms the upper half of the pipe clamp 10 and has a cap groove 26 that faces the saddle groove 18, so that the pipe clamp 10 has a cap groove facing the saddle groove 18. A first side of the cap 24 is pivotally connected to a first side of the base, and the cap 24 pivots between an open position and a closed position.

<!-- src: feature:F1, feature:F16, disclosure:§2, figure:FIG. 2, item:O5 -->
A spring 38 is placed between the base and the cap 24; the pipe clamp 10 thus has a spring arranged between the base and the cap 24. The spring 38 biases the cap 24 away from the base toward the open position: when nothing holds the cap 24, the spring 38 pushes the cap 24 open. In the embodiment of FIG. 2, with the cap 24 released, the spring 38 lifts the cap 24 by about 6 mm, so that a fitter can put the pipe 42 into the saddle groove 18 with one hand.

<!-- src: feature:F1, feature:F12, feature:F13, feature:F20, disclosure:§2, item:O5 -->
The pipe clamp 10 has a latch at a second side of the base, the free side opposite the first side. The latch is releasable and holds the cap 24 in the closed position against the spring 38. In the embodiment of FIG. 1 and FIG. 2, the latch is formed by a latch lug 32, a cap latch lug 30 and a locking pin 34, described below; in an alternative embodiment, the latch is a quarter-turn latch. The pipe clamp 10 is opened and closed without a tool and without a loose bolt.

<!-- src: feature:F9, feature:F10, inventor:IQ-1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O5 -->
In the embodiment shown, the cap 24 is a block 40 mm long and 40 mm wide, and the cap 24 is 22 mm high. The cap groove 26 is a half-round groove of 26 mm diameter on the underside of the cap 24 and matches the saddle groove 18. The cap groove 26 is 13 mm deep, half of 26 mm, so that 9 mm of material stays over the pipe 42. With the cap 24 in the closed position, the saddle groove 18 and the cap groove 26 together enclose the pipe 42, as FIG. 2 shows.

<!-- src: feature:F2, feature:F3, inventor:IQ-2, figure:FIG. 1, item:O6 -->
In the embodiment shown, the base comprises a base plate 12 and a saddle block 16. The base plate 12 is a flat steel plate 60 mm long, 40 mm wide and 8 mm thick. The 60 mm length of the base plate 12 runs across the pipe 42, from the hinge side to the latch side. The saddle block 16 sits in the middle, so that 10 mm of the base plate 12 is free at each side. Two mounting holes 14 of 6 mm diameter go through the base plate 12, one at each end. Each mounting hole 14 has its centre 6 mm from the end of the base plate 12 and 12 mm off the centre line towards the front face. The hinge lug 20 and the latch lug 32, described below, are 10 mm wide along the pipe 42 and sit at the middle of the block length, so that they cover only the centre line. A screwdriver reaches each mounting hole 14 from above, beside the lug.

<!-- src: feature:F4, feature:F5, feature:F6, figure:FIG. 1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O6 -->
The base thus has a saddle block on the base plate 12: the saddle block 16 sits on top of the base plate 12 and is 40 mm long along the pipe 42, 40 mm wide and 20 mm high. The saddle groove 18 is a half-round groove in the top of the saddle block 16, with a diameter of 26 mm, and runs along the direction of the pipe 42. The base plate 12 and the saddle block 16 are one machined part.

<!-- src: feature:F7, feature:F11, figure:FIG. 1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O7 -->
The pivotal connection of the cap 24 to the base is a hinge. The base has a hinge lug on the first side: the hinge lug 20 sits on one side of the saddle block 16, stands 12 mm above the top of the saddle block 16 and has a hole of 5 mm diameter along the direction of the pipe 42. The cap 24 has a cap hinge lug on the first side of the cap 24, the cap hinge lug 28.

<!-- src: feature:F8, inventor:IQ-3, figure:FIG. 1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O7 -->
The cap hinge lug 28 is a fork with two arms, each 8 mm wide along the pipe 42 and 12 mm high, one on each side of the hinge lug 20 with 2 mm clearance. The pipe clamp 10 has a hinge pin extending through the hinge lug 20 and the cap hinge lug 28. This hinge pin 22 is a steel pin of 5 mm diameter and 44 mm length, and the cap 24 pivots on the hinge pin 22. The hinge pin 22 is a press fit in the two arms of the cap hinge lug 28 and a running fit in the hinge lug 20; the press fit keeps the hinge pin 22 in place. The hinge pin 22 stands 7 mm out of each arm.

<!-- src: feature:F15, inventor:IQ-4, figure:FIG. 2, item:O8 -->
In the embodiment of FIG. 2, the spring 38 is a compression spring seated in a pocket 40 of the base. The pocket 40 is in the top of the saddle block 16, beside the saddle groove 18 at the second side of the base, the latch side. The pocket 40 is 6 mm in diameter and 6 mm deep, centred in the 7 mm land between the saddle groove 18 and the latch side face of the saddle block 16. The spring 38 has a coil diameter of 5 mm, a wire diameter of 0.8 mm and a free length of 12 mm. The built clamp has these sizes. As FIG. 2 shows, the spring 38 stands in the pocket 40 between the saddle block 16 and the cap 24.

<!-- src: feature:F21, disclosure:§6, inventor:IQ-5, item:O9 -->
In an alternative embodiment, not shown in the drawings, the spring is a leaf spring fixed to the base plate 12 in place of the spring 38. The leaf spring is a strip of spring steel, 0.5 mm thick, 10 mm wide and 30 mm long. One end of the strip is fixed under the head of the latch-side mounting screw on the top of the base plate 12, outside the saddle block 16. The strip bends up along the latch side face of the saddle block 16, and its free end bears under the cap latch lug 30. The leaf spring has not been built.

<!-- src: feature:F11, feature:F12, figure:FIG. 1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O10 -->
In the embodiment of FIG. 1 and FIG. 2, the latch comprises the latch lug 32, the cap latch lug 30 and the locking pin 34. The base has a latch lug on the second side: the latch lug 32 is on the free side of the saddle block 16 and has a hole receiving the locking pin 34, of 5 mm diameter along the direction of the pipe 42. The cap 24 has a cap latch lug on a second side of the cap 24, the cap latch lug 30, with a hole that lies in line with the hole of the latch lug 32 when the cap 24 is in the closed position.

<!-- src: feature:F13, figure:FIG. 1, figure:FIG. 2, item:O10 -->
The locking pin 34 is a steel pin of 5 mm diameter and 44 mm length. It has a head at one end with a diameter of 10 mm, the round head 36, which is a diameter larger than the 5 mm hole of the latch lug 32. The pipe clamp 10 thus has a locking pin removably insertable through the latch lug 32 and the cap latch lug 30 when the cap 24 is in the closed position: the fitter pushes the locking pin 34 through both lugs to hold the cap 24 closed and pulls it out to release the cap 24.

<!-- src: inventor:IQ-6, item:O10 -->
The locking pin 34 is a light press fit in the cap latch lug 30 and a running fit in the latch lug 32. The fitter pushes the locking pin 34 in with a thumb and pulls it out by the head 36. Friction holds the locking pin 34 in place; nothing else holds it.

<!-- src: feature:F20, disclosure:§6, inventor:IQ-7, item:O11 -->
In an alternative embodiment, not shown in the drawings, the latch is a quarter-turn latch on the free side, in place of the locking pin 34. A stud with a T-head stands up from the top of the latch lug 32. The cap latch lug 30 has a slot that the T-head passes through when the cap 24 closes. A quarter turn of the stud, by its knurled knob, sets the T-head across the slot, so that the T-head holds the cap latch lug 30 down against the spring 38. A quarter turn back releases it. The quarter-turn latch has not been built.

<!-- src: feature:F22, feature:F23, disclosure:§6, item:O12 -->
The pipe clamp 10 that was built and tested is made of steel. In an alternative embodiment for light pipes, the pipe clamp 10, including the base and the cap 24, is made of glass-filled nylon. A clamp of glass-filled nylon has not been built.

<!-- src: feature:F17, feature:F23, feature:F24, disclosure:§7, item:O13 -->
Example. The inventor built one steel pipe clamp 10 and fitted a steel pipe 42 of 25 mm outer diameter and 2 mm wall forty times on a wall board. Each fit took one hand, and no locking pin 34 was dropped. A pull of 400 N along the pipe 42 did not move the pipe 42.

<!-- src: inventor:IQ-8, item:O13 -->
The pipe clamp 10 is made in three sizes, for pipes of 20 mm, 25 mm and 32 mm outer diameter. The groove diameter is the pipe outer diameter plus 1 mm. Only the 25 mm size was built and tested.

<!-- src: feature:F19, disclosure:§5, figure:FIG. 3, item:O14 -->
FIG. 3 shows a method that secures a pipe in a clamp, for example the pipe 42 in the pipe clamp 10. In the clamp, the cap pivotally connected to the base by the hinge pin 22 is the cap 24, and the spring biasing the cap 24 away from the base is the spring 38. The method has the following steps in this order. In step 44, the pipe 42 is placed in the saddle groove 18, the half-round groove of the saddle block 16. In step 46, the cap 24 is pivoted about the hinge pin 22 onto the pipe 42. In step 48, the cap 24 compresses the spring 38. In step 50, the fitter pushes a locking pin through the latch lug 32 and the cap latch lug 30, here the locking pin 34. In step 52, the cap 24 is released, and the locking pin 34 holds the cap 24 closed against the spring 38.

<!-- src: feature:F18, disclosure:§4, item:O15 -->
In use, the fitter first fastens the base to a wall with screws through mounting holes 14 of the base plate 12, two screws in the embodiment shown. With the locking pin 34 out, the spring 38 holds the cap 24 open. The fitter puts the pipe 42 into the saddle groove 18 and presses the cap 24 down on the pipe 42 with one hand, so that the spring 38 compresses, and then pushes the locking pin 34 through the latch lug 32 and the cap latch lug 30.

<!-- src: feature:F18, disclosure:§4, item:O15 -->
To release the pipe 42, the fitter pulls the locking pin 34 out of the latch lug 32 and the cap latch lug 30, and the spring 38 lifts the cap 24 away from the pipe 42.

<!-- src: template, item:O16 -->
The embodiments above are described by way of example. Their features can be combined, and changes in form and detail can be made, within the scope of the claims that follow.

## CLAIMS

1. A pipe clamp, comprising: a base having a saddle groove configured to receive a pipe; a cap having a cap groove facing the saddle groove, a first side of the cap being pivotally connected to a first side of the base; a spring arranged between the base and the cap and biasing the cap away from the base toward an open position; and a latch at a second side of the base, the latch being releasable and configured to hold the cap in a closed position against the spring.

2. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the spring is a compression spring seated in a pocket of the base.

3. The pipe clamp of claim 2, wherein the pocket is located beside the saddle groove at the second side of the base.

4. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the latch comprises a latch lug on the second side of the base, a cap latch lug on a second side of the cap, and a locking pin removably insertable through the latch lug and the cap latch lug when the cap is in the closed position, the latch lug has a hole receiving the locking pin, and the locking pin has a head at one end with a diameter larger than the hole.

5. The pipe clamp of claim 1, further comprising a hinge pin extending through a hinge lug on the first side of the base and a cap hinge lug on the first side of the cap, the cap pivoting on the hinge pin.

6. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the base comprises a base plate having mounting holes and a saddle block on the base plate, the saddle groove is a half-round groove in a top of the saddle block, and the base plate and the saddle block are one machined part.

7. The pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the base and the cap are made of glass-filled nylon.

8. A method of securing a pipe in a clamp, the clamp comprising a base having a saddle groove, a cap pivotally connected to the base by a hinge pin, and a spring biasing the cap away from the base, the method comprising, in the following order: placing the pipe in the saddle groove; pivoting the cap about the hinge pin onto the pipe; compressing the spring with the cap; pushing a locking pin through a latch lug of the base and a cap latch lug of the cap; and releasing the cap, the locking pin holding the cap closed against the spring.

9. The method of claim 8, further comprising, before placing the pipe in the saddle groove, fastening the base to a wall with screws through mounting holes of the base.

10. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulling the locking pin out of the latch lug and the cap latch lug, the spring then lifting the cap away from the pipe.

## ABSTRACT

<!-- src: feature:F1, feature:F8, feature:F13, feature:F15, item:O17 -->
A pipe clamp has a base with a saddle groove that receives a pipe and a cap with a cap groove facing the saddle groove. One side of the cap is pivotally connected to one side of the base, for example by a hinge pin through lugs of the base and the cap. A spring between the base and the cap, for example a compression spring in a pocket of the base, pushes the cap open when nothing holds it. A releasable latch at the other side of the base holds the cap closed against the spring, for example a locking pin pushed through a latch lug of the base and a cap latch lug of the cap. A fitter places the pipe in the saddle groove, pivots the cap onto the pipe and pushes the locking pin in with one hand, without a tool or a loose bolt.
